thread.document:
I made a very small Jupyter notebook called diffpool_visualizer.ipynb that acts as a conceptual DiffPool visualizer. Instead of training a big GNN, it focuses only on the core DiffPool step:

We build a tiny toy graph (two triangles connected by a bridge).

We define a soft assignment matrix S from nodes to clusters (what DiffPool would learn in practice).

We compute:

New cluster features 

$$X_{pooled}=S^TX$$

A coarsened adjacency 

$$A_{pooled}=S^TAS$$

We then visualize three things side by side:

Original graph: each node is colored by how strongly it belongs to a chosen cluster (you can switch clusters with a slider).

Assignment matrix S: shown as a heatmap (rows = nodes, columns = clusters).

Coarsened graph: a tiny graph whose nodes are clusters, with edge thickness showing how strongly clusters are connected.

How to use it

Open diffpool_visualizer.ipynb in a Jupyter environment.

Run all cells.

Use the cluster index slider under the last cell:

Watch how the colors on the original graph change as you switch clusters.

Compare that to the corresponding column in the assignment matrix S.

Look at how many cluster nodes there are and how they are connected in the coarsened graph.
